text:
Tom: Heads-up: SkyNode (hardware marketplace partner) is ready to start sending usage to our marketplace webhook. They have a funky timezone behavior (device local time) and sometimes send midnight-aligned buckets in their local tz. We need to decide normalization + crediting semantics before onboarding.

Lena: Good catch. We should normalize to UTC hour buckets on ingest and keep original_device_ts for reconciliation. What about daylight savings shifts? Some devices report local tz without offset.

Diego: Proposal: require iso8601 with offset. If partner sends naive local timestamps, reject with 422 and ask for timezone or send metadata header X-Device-TZ. Fallback: if a device historically sends naive timestamps, allow opt-in heuristic mapping for that device only (audit logged).

Kara: Metering detail: SkyNode reports "active_minutes" per hour per device (integer 0-60). We bill per-minute as compute_unit_minutes. Need mapping active_minutes -> compute_unit_minutes and ledger rows in minutes. Also support conversion to hours in downstream invoices.

Tom: Sample payload they sent: ```json
{
  "node_id": "sn-9001",
  "local_ts": "2026-03-28T00:00:00",
  "tz": "America/Chicago",
  "active_minutes": 45,
  "sku": "SN-CORE"
}
```
They sometimes batch by day with an array of hour entries.

Priya: Backend requirements:
- Normalize: convert local_ts + tz -> UTC hour bucket and store original_ts + tz
- Dedupe key: partner_id + node_id + utc_hour_bucket
- Accept out-of-order up to 96h for SkyNode by contract; default partners 72h.
- If replay affects a previously closed billing period -> create an adjustment entry with tag adjustment_reason: "late_replay" and create FIN ticket.

Diego: Edge case: DST spring-forward can make an hour missing; devices may still send an hour bucket labeled "00:00" twice (ambiguous). Rule: require tz offset on the event or tz field. If ambiguous and no offset, reject. If they include tz like America/Chicago we resolve using IANA rules for that timestamp.

Kara: On credits: Business wants to avoid auto-crediting unless the delta is material. Proposed policy: if replay causes net delta < 1% of partner hourly volume OR < 5 minutes total for the affected partner-hour, auto-apply without finance ticket. Otherwise create adjustment_pending and surface to finance for approval.

metering-bot: Lint: sample payload missing offset but contains tz field 'America/Chicago' -> passes heuristics (sha256:deadbeef).

Tom: Can we have partner-side hourly rollups? If SkyNode provides signed daily rollups we can use as secondary source for reconciliation. Kara?

Kara: Yes, ask them to include daily_rollup with fields {hour_utc, total_active_minutes, signature}. Reconciliation job will compare ledger minute-sums vs partner rollups per utc_hour. Alert thresholds: >0.7% OR >10 minutes absolute.

Priya: API behavior and codes: 202 Accepted (include accepted_count and canonical_utc_hours), 400 malformed, 401 invalid-key, 409 duplicate (return ingest_ts), 422 tz-ambiguous (explain missing offset). Rate-limit SkyNode to 120 req/s and per-node burst 20 req/min.

Diego: Tests: timezone-aware buckets, DST fall-back / spring-forward, naive timestamp rejection path, large day-batch pagination, late-arrival adjustment generation. I'll add unit vectors.

Tom: Action items: Lena (document tz normalization + heuristic opt-in flow), Priya (adapter + 96h grace per contract), Kara (reconciliation + thresholds + finance integration), Diego (tests + dedupe helper), SkyNode PM (provide signed rollups and confirm tz behavior). Sync Thursday 11am.

SkyNode PM (via email): We will send tz in payload and can include signed rollups. Thanks, will confirm rollup schema by EOD.

Tom: :+1: Closing this thread; we'll publish a short onboarding runbook for SkyNode with these rules.
